tasks.short: Write or check the spec for a new HR report or Power BI dashboard before it is built.

today.trigger: An HR Business Partner, the HR Director or Finance asks for a new report or a change to an existing Power BI dashboard.
steps: Meet the requester to pin down the question the report answers and who will see it
Look up AFAS Profit tables, fields and existing measure definitions in the nightly extract
Write the spec in SharePoint: sources, joins, DAX measures, filters, row-level security, refresh
Check the spec against privacy rules (no absence causes, minimum group size) and works council agreements
Review specs or model changes written by others before they go live
drudgery: Copying field names and table structures from AFAS into the document
Rewriting the same definitions (FTE, headcount, verzuim rate, 90-day retention) in every spec
Keeping old documentation in step with dashboards that have changed
today.time_sinks: Finding out how a field or measure is actually computed in the current model, and chasing the requester for a precise definition.

lenses.faster: Copilot reads the Power BI semantic model and the AFAS extract schema and drafts the field list, joins, DAX and refresh section; the analyst writes purpose, privacy rules and edge cases and reviews, taking a spec from about a day to a few hours.
lenses.autonomous: When a dataset is published or changed, a script regenerates the data dictionary and lineage page from model metadata and flags measures that drifted from the agreed metric list; the analyst approves before the page is replaced.
lenses.ambitious: New service: a plain-language metric glossary for the three HR Business Partners and site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, so they know what each number means; demand grows as more managers and chat agents query the model.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping field lists and chasing stale documentation; the analyst wants more time agreeing definitions with HR and Finance and designing what a report should answer.
lenses.options: Drafting two or three report designs (e.g. 90-day retention by hire cohort vs by site and agency) before build lets the requester pick the view that fits the decision, not just the first one built.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from writing documents to running the metric layer: the analyst decides which definitions are canonical, which fields may be exposed and at what group size, and signs off every model change; the job becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's documentation of shared HR cost and FTE measures in finance dashboards; needs basic finance chart-of-accounts knowledge in AFAS
Absorb the HR Administrator's field-definition questions on AFAS data entry; needs AFAS Profit configuration knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the requester really needs to decide, which AFAS fields are unreliable at which site, and where a report would breach GDPR Art. 9 or need works council consent under WOR 27.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst leads the design and judgement calls; AI drafts the mechanical parts of the spec from model metadata, which a person must check because Copilot can misread an unprepared model.

in_practice.trigger: A report request is logged, or a change is published to the Power BI semantic model.
steps: Pull model metadata (tables, measures, relationships, RLS roles) and the request text
Copilot drafts the spec sections: sources, joins, DAX, refresh, data dictionary
A deterministic check compares measures with the agreed metric list and flags health-data fields
Analyst adds purpose, privacy and edge cases, edits and approves
Approved spec is saved to SharePoint and linked from the dashboard
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves every spec and any change to a canonical metric definition before build or publication.
systems: Power BI (Copilot, Fabric or Premium capacity)
data_needed: Privacy rules and works council agreements on HR reporting
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint documentation library with version history

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX and summarises reports on a semantic model, but can misinterpret data without a prepared model; non-English chat not officially supported.
Text-to-SQL cut query authoring from about 10 to 3 minutes, but hallucinated tables and columns remain unsolved.
Generating data dictionaries from model metadata via scripts (e.g. Tabular Editor, DMVs) is standard practice.

risks: Draft spec invents a field or misstates a measure and the error is built into the dashboard
Spec exposes small groups or absence detail, breaching GDPR Art. 9 or a works council agreement
Fabric or Premium capacity cost needed for Copilot may not be justified at this volume
research_questions: Does Noordhaven's Power BI tenant run on Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity so Copilot is available at all?
How many specs per year are written, and how long does each take today?
What share of Copilot-drafted DAX and field lists needs correction on the HR model?
Does the works council agreement on HR reporting already define minimum group sizes the check can enforce?

tasks.short: Scan HR tech and labour market trends to decide which new HR analytics services or tools to offer.

today.trigger: A quarterly planning cycle, a vendor pitch, or the HR Director asks whether a new tool (e.g. AI in Recruitee or Power BI) is worth it.
steps: Read vendor updates, analyst reports, newsletters and peer posts on HR tech and the logistics labour market
Note what AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft are releasing
Compare with Noordhaven's gaps (time to hire, flex worker data, verzuim reporting)
Write a short note or slide for the HR Director with options and a recommendation
drudgery: Wading through vendor marketing to find what a feature actually does
Rewriting the same background in every note
today.time_sinks: Reading many sources to separate vendor claims from documented results, and checking whether a feature works in Dutch and under AVG.

lenses.faster: A model collects and summarises release notes and reports on a fixed source list, with links and a caveat for each claim; the analyst reads a two-page digest and checks the few items that matter, roughly halving the time.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly, a scheduled job pulls the source list, drafts a digest graded by evidence (vendor claim, product live, documented case) and posts it to a Teams channel; the analyst approves before it goes to the HR Director.
lenses.ambitious: Decisions made far more often: a short go/no-go note for every relevant release from AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft, not just the one or two a year that get attention today; demand grows if cheaper because vendors ship monthly.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses wading through vendor marketing; the analyst wants more time testing promising features on Noordhaven data and talking with HR colleagues about what would help them.
lenses.options: Laying out two or three options side by side (wait, pilot on one site, buy) with cost, evidence grade and works council impact changes which choice the HR Director makes.
lenses.altitude: The analyst becomes the HR team's adviser on analytics and AI tooling: they set the source list and evidence bar, run small pilots, and own the recommendation on which tools reach the works council for consent; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb part of the HR Director's vendor screening for HR tech; needs procurement and contract basics
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's scan of Studytube and learning tech features; needs learning design basics

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a trend fits Noordhaven's shift workforce, CAO, sites and data quality, spotting vendor claims with no customer result, and weighing works council and EU AI Act consequences.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call per batch turns a fixed set of sources into a graded, linked summary inside a fixed monthly workflow; the steps are predictable, so an agent is not needed.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule, or an ad hoc question from the HR Director about a specific tool.
steps: Fetch new items from a fixed source list (vendor release notes, regulator pages, chosen analyst sources)
Model summarises each item with link, evidence grade and caveats (Dutch support, AVG, AI Act category)
Model drafts a digest with options for Noordhaven's open gaps
Analyst checks claims against the sources, adds the recommendation and approves
Digest is posted to the HR Teams channel and stored in SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst verifies each claim used in a recommendation and approves the digest before it reaches the HR Director.
data_needed: Noordhaven's list of open HR analytics gaps and current tool contracts
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint folder of monthly digests with source links

evidence.claim: Trend reports from vendors do not establish causation; caveats must be kept.
Vendor productivity claims like Visier's '10x' come without a named customer result.
Self-reported AI use is exaggerated by 48% of surveyed employees, so survey-based trend data runs high.
From 2 Dec 2027 AI that allocates tasks or evaluates performance is high-risk under Annex III 4(b).

risks: Summaries repeat vendor claims as facts and lead to a poor purchase
Model misses or misdates regulatory changes (AI Act timelines, AP guidance)
Digest grows into reading nobody acts on
research_questions: How many tool decisions per year does HR make, and how many were preceded by a written trend note?
Can the analyst find a source list small enough to keep checking yet covering AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft releases?
In a three-month trial, how many summarised claims fail the analyst's source check?
Does the HR Director act on a monthly digest, or only on ad hoc notes?

role.altitude: From building reports and notes on request to owning Noordhaven's HR metric layer and tool choices: canonical definitions, access and group-size rules, model checks, and the evidence bar for new HR analytics tools, with sign-off on what managers and agents may query.
reach: FP&A Analyst: HR cost and FTE measures in finance dashboards
HR Administrator: AFAS data quality checks and field definitions
HR Business Partner: answering routine manager questions on headcount, verzuim and retention via a governed Q&A
HR Director: first screening of HR tech vendors and pilots
role.ceiling_note: About 96 hours a year sit in these two tasks; savings of 40 to 45% free roughly 40 hours. The limit is judgement: definitions, privacy and works council consent, and fit with Noordhaven's shift workforce cannot be delegated, and Power BI Copilot needs Fabric or Premium capacity and a prepared model.
skills_to_grow: Semantic model design and governance in Power BI (verified answers, RLS, metadata scripting)
Evaluating LLM output against sources and model metadata
GDPR Art. 9, WOR 27 and EU AI Act basics for HR analytics
Vendor assessment and small pilot design
role.ambitious_version: Run a governed HR metric layer that lets HR Business Partners and site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get correct answers on 90-day retention, verzuim and flex-worker use themselves, with every definition documented and every tool choice backed by a graded monthly evidence digest.
